text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An agreement signed between Russia's diamond-rich republic of Sakha-Yakutia and Belarus will allow Yakutian authorities to tighten control over raw stones circulation on the markets of the Commonwealth of Independent States.
- Privatisation of Russia's oil industry is entering its final stage.
- Russian bankers criticise the Central Bank and Savings Bank for their position on commercial banks and on laws regulating Russia's banking system.
- Federation Council upper parliament house supports government's housing reform.
- France's PSA Peugeot Citroen company is studying possibilities to assemble Peugeot cars in Russia.
- Sergei Stepashin, former Federal Security Service chief and the newly appointed Justice Minister, has retained a great influence on security structures.
- Azeri President Haydar Aliyev has emerged as a mediator in complicated talks between Russia and Chechnya.
- Enivironmental situation in Moscow is getting worse as piles of garbage and industrial waste grow around the city.
- Diamonds of Russia-Sakha company is allowed to resume exports after Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin signed an annual quota resolution.
- Russia's Central Bank softens some regulations for foreigners willing to invest into charter capital of Russian banks, says Sergei Dubinin, the head of the Central bank.
- Success of talks between Russia and Chechnya depends to a great extent on the position of Azeri President.
- Russia is planning to change the structure of its grain imports, grain experts say.
